transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO, Oceanridge), Liam (Head of Platform), Aisha (Security), Eduardo (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (sometimes noisy):
Oceanridge wants to extend commitment, add capacity and a second region (eu-west), consider private VPC pilot with KMS, ask about latency tradeoffs and burst pricing.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time today. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Shah: Hi, Priya here.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam on my side.
[00:10] Aisha Malik: Aisha.
[00:11] Eduardo Reyes: Eduardo.
[00:13] Jonah Ruiz: Jonah from Redwood.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Cool. Sit rep: we heard you want to lock into a 12-month renewal and carve out a burst pattern for Black Friday-ish traffic, and also start EU onboarding. Wanted to walk through the plan and any blockers.
[00:31] Priya Shah: Yes exactly. We liked the dedicated pool from the pilot but our infra team wants to avoid a big upfront commit, so thinking about a baseline plus a "staggered burst" model where we keep modest reserved and a priced burst band.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: Two pieces: residency — EU region for customer-facing features — and we need to know expected p95 on the dedicated baseline vs burst. Also, how do you do automatic fallback if burst capacity isn't available?
[00:59] Jonah Ruiz: Good q. On p95 we usually see baseline dedicated at x ms p95 for 8k tokens workloads — sorry the auto transcript mangled that — but more concretely, for the family of models you're using (redwood-compatible Llama variants) we expect p95 in the 120–220ms range for token gen on A100-style hardware for short sequences; burst will add queueing, but we provide priority routing and optional regional fallback.
[01:28] Aisha Malik: Need to call out security — we have requirements around KMS, audit logs retained 7 years, and proof of SOC2. Can you confirm redaction and egress?
[01:41] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We have standard SOC2 docs and can share our security pack. For the private VPC pilot we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) and we can enable detailed audit logs. On redaction, we have guidance but final masking has to be in your pipeline — the service can do token-level pseudonymization if needed, but it's not a replacement for pre-send scrubbing.
[02:05] Eduardo Reyes: Quick technical: how does KV cache behave with multi-region? If we have eu-west plus us-west, will the KV sync add latency?
[02:17] Jonah Ruiz: Short answer: KV cache is per-serving cluster to keep latency low. We don't sync hot KV across regions; instead requests can be routed by policy. So eu requests hit eu cluster with warm caches, us requests hit us. There is a consistency tradeoff but it's standard. The transcript may say K-V cash earlier which is funny.
[02:36] Priya Shah: If we route by policy and do fallbacks, what's the user impact if fallback goes to US? Data residency concerns.
[02:44] Jonah Ruiz: You can set strict routing to prevent cross-region fallback. Alternatively we can do sanitized fallback where only non-PII requests are eligible. We'll put that configuration in the SOW.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: Pricing: baseline reserved commit 100 infer/sec; burst up to 400 for short bursts. What's the billing cadence for burst? Hourly? Minute-level?
[03:11] Maya Patel: We propose minute-level burst billing with a rate multiplier. For the staggered burst concept: Tier 1 baseline reserved, Tier 2 predictable scheduled bursts (e.g., nightly batch), Tier 3 on-demand with higher multiplier. We'll include examples in the SOW so you can model cost.
[03:30] Priya Shah: Are there examples from other financial customers about cost variability?
[03:34] Maya Patel: We can share anonymized usage curves — not exact dollars but patterns. Also Redwood Optimize recommendations can suggest quantization profiles for burst to reduce token cost while preserving quality.
[03:47] Aisha Malik: On KMS, who holds the keys? Do you support HSM-based BYOK?
[03:52] Jonah Ruiz: Yes BYOK + HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted API also supports customer-managed keys in many cases; we'll confirm specifics for EU deployment.
[04:05] Priya Shah: SLAs — we're trying to push for a p95 of 250ms for standard paths. Is that feasible with the model choices and eu-onboarding?
[04:14] Jonah Ruiz: With dedicated pools pinned to your workload and warm caches, p95 250ms is achievable for short contexts. For long-context or heavy attention models it increases — we'll pin the model family in SOW.
[04:27] Liam O'Connor: Procurement: our finance team wants a single invoice monthly and a way to correlate spend to teams. Does Redwood provide token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[04:38] Maya Patel: Yes the Console gives token-level and route-level cost. We can set up role-based dashboards for your billing owners.
[04:45] Priya Shah: On the EU timeline, we wanted to be live before end of Q1 2026. Is that doable?
[04:52] Maya Patel: Timeline seems reasonable: EU provisioning, VPC peering, and pilot can fit in ~10–12 weeks once SOW signed and we have networking contacts.
[04:59] Eduardo Reyes: Network-wise we'll need a breakout doc for egress IP ranges and peering steps.
[05:03] Jonah Ruiz: We'll share a dry-run playbook and a short checklist for your infra team.
[05:09] [short pause, cross talk]
[05:15] Priya Shah: One last thing: we evaluated competitor quotes from Anthropic and Databricks — their pricing on burst looked cheaper but they didn't meet our KMS+private pilot constraints. Can you give any leverage on the multiplier?
[05:29] Maya Patel: We can be pragmatic in SOW; the multiplier can be tiered and there's room to trade some baseline commit for lower burst rates. We'll model three scenarios in the doc.
[05:39] Aisha Malik: On compliance, we need log retention to meet audits. Can you commit to 7 years?
[05:45] Jonah Ruiz: We can retain audit logs per contract; long-term retention is an add-on due to storage cost but it's available. We'll include a line item.
[05:55] Priya Shah: Great. Next steps again?
[05:58] Maya Patel: We'll send: 1) revised SOW with tiered pricing; 2) security pack and SOC2; 3) benchmark plan; 4) schedule for technical deep-dive.
[06:09] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. Prefer doc by Friday so we can start procurement.
[06:12] Maya Patel: We'll aim for Friday (2025-11-21).
[06:15] [closing remarks]
[06:18] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
[06:23] Priya Shah: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
